claim: Increased adrenergic tone resulting from cardiovascular stress leads to development of heart failure, in part, through chronic stimulation of β1 adrenergic receptors (βARs) on cardiac myocytes.
source: Increased adrenergic tone resulting from cardiovascular stress leads to development of heart failure, in part, through chronic stimulation of β1 adrenergic receptors (βARs) on cardiac myocytes.
evidence: This claim is supported by established scientific knowledge about cardiovascular disease mechanisms and is stated in the abstract.

claim: Blocking β1 adrenergic receptors is part of the basis for β-blocker therapy for heart failure.
source: Blocking these receptors is part of the basis for β-blocker therapy for heart failure.
evidence: This claim is supported by established clinical knowledge about β-blocker therapy.

claim: G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs), including βARs, are activated intracellularly.
source: Recent data demonstrate that G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs), including βARs, are activated intracellularly, although the biological significance is unclear.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to recent data in the field.

claim: Golgi βARs in rat cardiac myocytes activate Golgi localized, prohypertrophic, phosphoinositide hydrolysis.
source: Here we investigated the functional role of Golgi βARs in rat cardiac myocytes and found they activate Golgi localized, prohypertrophic, phosphoinositide hydrolysis, that is not accessed by cell surface βAR stimulation.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Cell surface βAR stimulation does not access Golgi localized phosphoinositide hydrolysis.
source: Here we investigated the functional role of Golgi βARs in rat cardiac myocytes and found they activate Golgi localized, prohypertrophic, phosphoinositide hydrolysis, that is not accessed by cell surface βAR stimulation.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data.

claim: The Golgi βAR pathway is accessed by norepinephrine via an Oct3 organic cation transporter.
source: This pathway is accessed by the physiological neurotransmitter norepinephrine (NE) via an Oct3 organic cation transporter.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data using Oct3 inhibitors.

claim: Blockade of Oct3 prevents NE dependent cardiac myocyte hypertrophy.
source: Blockade of Oct3 or specific blockade of Golgi resident β1ARs prevents NE dependent cardiac myocyte hypertrophy.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data showing Oct3 inhibitors block NE-induced hypertrophy.

claim: Specific blockade of Golgi resident β1ARs prevents NE dependent cardiac myocyte hypertrophy.
source: Blockade of Oct3 or specific blockade of Golgi resident β1ARs prevents NE dependent cardiac myocyte hypertrophy.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data using Nb80 nanobody targeting.

claim: Cardiovascular diseases, including heart failure, are the leading cause of disease and death in the developed world.
source: Cardiovascular diseases, including heart failure, are the leading cause of disease and death in the developed world.
evidence: This is established epidemiological knowledge.

claim: Long term pathological stress such as hypertension or myocardial infarction increases levels of neurohumoral factors such as epinephrine, endothelin and angiotensin II.
source: In response to long term pathological stress, such as hypertension or myocardial infarction, the levels of neurohumoral factors such as epinephrine, endothelin and angiotensin II increase.
evidence: This is supported by established knowledge and citations in the field.

claim: Neurohumoral factors directly stimulate G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs), including β-adrenergic receptors in cardiac myocytes.
source: These hormones directly stimulate G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs), including β-adrenergic receptors in cardiac myocytes (D'Angelo et al., 1997; Adams et al., 1998; Rockman et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Chronic stimulation of β-adrenergic receptors by catecholamines drives cardiac hypertrophy and ventricular remodeling, ultimately leading to heart failure.
source: Chronic stimulation of these receptors, including stimulation of β-adrenergic receptors (βARs) by catecholamines, drives cardiac hypertrophy and ventricular remodeling, ultimately leading to heart failure.
evidence: This is supported by established knowledge in cardiovascular pathophysiology.

claim: The efficacy of β-blocker therapy for treatment of heart failure results, at least in part, by ameliorating chronic βAR stimulation in the heart.
source: The efficacy of β-blocker therapy for treatment of heart failure results, at least in part, by ameliorating chronic βAR stimulation in the heart (Bristow, 2000; Wang et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to clinical research.

claim: PLCβ isoforms stimulated by Gq have been implicated in cardiac hypertrophy driven by cell surface α-adrenergic receptors.
source: PLCβ isoforms stimulated by Gq have been implicated in cardiac hypertrophy driven by cell surface α-adrenergic receptors (αAR) (Filtz et al., 2009; Grubb et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: PLCε plays a critical role in cardiac hypertrophy driven downstream of the endothelin (ET-1A) receptor and cAMP signaling by βARs.
source: Our laboratory identified a critical role of PLCε in cardiac hypertrophy driven downstream of the endothelin (ET-1A) receptor and cAMP signaling by βARs (Zhang et al., 2011; Zhang et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work from the authors' laboratory.

claim: PLCε has diverse upstream regulators including heterotrimeric G protein βγ subunits and small GTPases, including Rap, Rho and Ras, and cAMP via the Rap guanine nucleotide exchange factor (GEF), Epac.
source: PLCε is poised as a nexus for multiple receptor signaling systems due to its diversity of upstream regulators including heterotrimeric G protein βγ subunits and small GTPases, including Rap, Rho and Ras, and cAMP via the Rap guanine nucleotide exchange factor (GEF), Epac (Kelley et al., 2004; Malik et al., 2015; Kelley et al., 2001; Harden and Sondek, 2006; Smrcka et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous research.

claim: PLCε and Epac are scaffolded together at the nuclear envelope in cardiac myocytes by the hypertrophic organizer, muscle-specific A kinase anchoring protein (mAKAPβ), in close proximity to the Golgi apparatus.
source: PLCε and Epac are scaffolded together at the nuclear envelope in cardiac myocytes by the hypertrophic organizer, muscle-specific A kinase anchoring protein (mAKAPβ), in close proximity to the Golgi apparatus (Dodge-Kafka et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: Activation of PLCε in cardiac myocytes induces hydrolysis of phosphatidylinositol-4-phosphate (PI4P) at the Golgi apparatus leading to release of diacylglycerol (DAG) and inactive IP2 in the vicinity of the nucleus to facilitate nuclear protein kinase D (PKD) and subsequent downstream hypertrophic pathways.
source: Activation of PLCε in cardiac myocytes induces hydrolysis of phosphatidylinositol-4-phosphate (PI4P) at the Golgi apparatus leading to release of diacylglycerol (DAG) and inactive IP2 in the vicinity of the nucleus to facilitate nuclear protein kinase D (PKD) and subsequent downstream hypertrophic pathways (Zhang et al., 2013; Vega et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The Epac-selective cAMP analog, cpTOME, activates PLCε-dependent Golgi PI4P hydrolysis in cardiac myocytes.
source: In previous work we found that either the Epac-selective cAMP analog, cpTOME, or forskolin stimulation of adenylate cyclase, activate PLCε-dependent Golgi PI4P hydrolysis in cardiac myocytes.
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work from the authors' laboratory.

claim: Forskolin stimulation of adenylate cyclase activates PLCε-dependent Golgi PI4P hydrolysis in cardiac myocytes.
source: In previous work we found that either the Epac-selective cAMP analog, cpTOME, or forskolin stimulation of adenylate cyclase, activate PLCε-dependent Golgi PI4P hydrolysis in cardiac myocytes.
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work from the authors' laboratory.

claim: The βAR agonist isoproterenol does not stimulate Golgi PI4P hydrolysis despite strongly stimulating cAMP production.
source: Surprisingly, the βAR agonist isoproterenol (Iso), does not stimulate Golgi PI4P hydrolysis despite strongly stimulating cAMP production (Nash et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work from the authors' laboratory.

claim: PLCε-dependent PI4P hydrolysis can be controlled by two distinct pools of cAMP delimited by distinct PDE isoforms.
source: As an explanation for this apparent paradox we demonstrated PLCε-dependent PI4P hydrolysis can be controlled by two distinct pools of cAMP delimited by distinct PDE isoforms.
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work from the authors' laboratory.

claim: One pool of cAMP, limited by PDE3, acts through Epac and Rap1 to activate PLCε.
source: One pool, limited by PDE3 acts through Epac and Rap1 to activate PLCε, while a second pool controlled by PDE2 and/or PDE9A inhibits PLCε activity through activation of PKA (Nash et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work from the authors' laboratory.

claim: A second pool of cAMP controlled by PDE2 and/or PDE9A inhibits PLCε activity through activation of PKA.
source: One pool, limited by PDE3 acts through Epac and Rap1 to activate PLCε, while a second pool controlled by PDE2 and/or PDE9A inhibits PLCε activity through activation of PKA (Nash et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work from the authors' laboratory.

claim: cAMP generated downstream of Iso cannot access the Epac/mAKAPβ/PLCε complex unless PDE3 is specifically inhibited.
source: cAMP generated downstream of Iso cannot access the Epac/mAKAPβ/PLCε complex unless PDE3 is specifically inhibited, partially explaining the lack of activation of Golgi PI4P hydrolysis by Iso.
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work from the authors' laboratory.

claim: GPCRs in different intracellular compartments have discrete signaling outputs.
source: A new paradigm for generating localized cAMP signals in cells has been established by a number of recent studies indicating that GPCRs in different intracellular compartments have discrete signaling outputs (Vilardaga et al., 2014; Irannejad et al., 2017; Irannejad et al., 2013; Irannejad and von Zastrow, 2014; Stoeber et al., 2018; Calebiro et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to recent research.

claim: βARs internalized into endosomes continue to stimulate cAMP accumulation resulting in cellular outcomes distinct from those generated by βARs at the cell surface.
source: An emergent idea is that βARs internalized into endosomes continue to stimulate cAMP accumulation resulting in cellular outcomes distinct from those generated by βARs at the cell surface.
evidence: This is supported by inference from cited literature on intracellular GPCR signaling.

claim: β1ARs expressed at the Golgi apparatus in HeLa cells can induce G protein activation in the Golgi when stimulated by either a cell permeant agonist, dobutamine, through passive diffusion, or the physiological hormone epinephrine, when transported across the cell membrane by the organic cation transporter, Oct3.
source: Irannejad et al. (2017) established that β1ARs expressed at the Golgi apparatus in HeLa cells can induce G protein activation in the Golgi when stimulated by either a cell permeant agonist, dobutamine, through passive diffusion, or the physiological hormone epinephrine, when transported across the cell membrane by the organic cation transporter, Oct3.
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: Dobutamine stimulated rapid and sustained PI4P hydrolysis in NRVMs.
source: In contrast to Iso, dobutamine stimulated rapid and sustained PI4P hydrolysis (Figure 1A, left).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Metoprolol blocked dobutamine-stimulated PI4P hydrolysis.
source: Addition of metoprolol, but not sotalol, blocked dobutamine-stimulated PI4P hydrolysis (Figure 1A middle and right panels).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Sotalol did not block dobutamine-stimulated PI4P hydrolysis.
source: Addition of metoprolol, but not sotalol, blocked dobutamine-stimulated PI4P hydrolysis (Figure 1A middle and right panels).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Stimulation of an intracellular population of βARs is required for dobutamine-mediated PI4P hydrolysis.
source: This indicates that stimulation of an intracellular population βARs is required for dobutamine-mediated PI4P hydrolysis.
evidence: This is an inference based on the differential effects of membrane-permeant vs impermeant antagonists.

claim: Dobutamine caused rapid clearance of cytoplasmic NES-Venus-mini-Gs fluorescence and accumulation at the PM and punctate structures.
source: Addition of dobutamine to cells co-expressing NES-Venus-mini-Gs and FLAG-β1AR, caused a rapid clearance of cytoplasmic fluorescence and accumulated fluorescence at the PM and punctate structures, possibly corresponding to microtubules.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Dobutamine caused slower translocation of Venus associated fluorescence to the perinuclear region of the cell colocalizing with CFP-giantin, a marker for the Golgi apparatus.
source: This was followed by slower translocation of Venus associated fluorescence to the perinuclear region of the cell colocalizing with the CFP-giantin, a marker for the Golgi apparatus (Figure 1B,D and E and Figure 1—video 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B, D, and E.

claim: Iso caused rapid translocation of NES-Venus-mini-Gs to the PM but no accumulation at the perinuclear region.
source: Iso also caused rapid translocation to the PM but, in contrast to dobutamine, no accumulation at the perinuclear region was observed (Figure 1C,D and E and Figure 1—video 2).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C, D, and E.

claim: Brefeldin A treatment significantly reversed NES-Venus-mini-Gs association with the perinuclear region, confirming Golgi localization.
source: Brefeldin A treatment significantly reversed NES-Venus-mini-Gs association with the perinuclear region, confirming Golgi localization of NES-Venus-mini-Gs (Figure 1—figure supplement 2 and Figure 1—video 3).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: A population of βARs present at the Golgi can be activated by exogenous agonists and stimulate Gs, ultimately resulting in PLC activation and PI4P hydrolysis.
source: Taken together, these data support the idea that a population of βARs present at the Golgi can be activated by exogenous agonists and stimulate Gs, ultimately resulting in PLC activation and PI4P hydrolysis.
evidence: This is an inference based on the combined experimental data from Figure 1.

claim: PLCε (PLCE1) shRNA depletion of PLCε completely inhibited PI4P hydrolysis stimulated by dobutamine.
source: PLCε (PLCE1) shRNA depletion of PLCε completely inhibited PI4P hydrolysis stimulated by dobutamine, while negative control (NC) scrambled shRNA had no effect (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Viral expression of the PLCε RA1 domain inhibited PI4P hydrolysis stimulated by dobutamine.
source: Viral expression of the PLCε RA1 domain also inhibited PI4P hydrolysis stimulated by dobutamine (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: mAKAPβ-scaffolded PLCε is required for dobutamine-mediated PI4P hydrolysis.
source: This demonstrates that mAKAPβ- scaffolded PLCε is required for dobutamine-mediated PI4P hydrolysis.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data showing RA1 domain disruption of the mAKAPβ-PLCε complex blocks dobutamine effects.

claim: The Epac-selective inhibitor HJC0726 inhibited PI4P hydrolysis stimulated by dobutamine.
source: The Epac-selective inhibitor HJC0726 inhibited (Zhu et al., 2015) PI4P hydrolysis stimulated by dobutamine (Figure 2C)
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The βγ inhibitor Gallein had no effect on dobutamine-stimulated PI4P hydrolysis.
source: however, the βγ inhibitor Gallein had no effect (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Golgi PI4P hydrolysis stimulated by intracellular GPCRs requires the Epac/mAKAPβ/PLCε complex.
source: Taken together, these data indicate that Golgi PI4P hydrolysis stimulated by intracellular GPCRs requires the Epac/mAKAPβ/PLCε complex.
evidence: This is an inference based on the combined experimental data from Figure 2.

claim: Following addition of 1 μM Rapamycin, dobutamine-induced PI4P hydrolysis was significantly inhibited.
source: However, following addition of 1 μM Rapamycin, dobutamine-induced PI4P hydrolysis was significantly inhibited (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: βARs expressed directly on the Golgi are required for dobutamine-mediated PI4P hydrolysis at the Golgi.
source: These data confirm that βARs expressed directly on the Golgi are required for dobutamine-mediated PI4P hydrolysis at the Golgi.
evidence: This is an inference based on the Nb80 translocation experiment blocking dobutamine effects.

claim: CGP-20172 completely blocked dobutamine-stimulated PI4P hydrolysis.
source: CGP-20172 completely blocked dobutamine-stimulated PI4P hydrolysis (Figure 3C)
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Dobutamine stimulation of Golgi localized PI4P hydrolysis is through Golgi localized β1ARs.
source: indicating that the dobutamine stimulation of Golgi localized PI4P hydrolysis is through Golgi localized β1ARs.
evidence: This is an inference based on the β1AR-selective antagonist blocking dobutamine effects.

claim: NE caused delayed, but robust PI4P hydrolysis in NRVMs at 37°C.
source: NE caused delayed, but robust PI4P hydrolysis (Figure 4A, left).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: PI4P hydrolysis initiated by NE was blocked by metoprolol but not sotalol.
source: PI4P hydrolysis initiated by NE was blocked by metoprolol (100 μM, Figure 4A, center) but not sotalol (5 mM, Figure 4A, right) indicating that NE can stimulate internal βARs.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: NE can stimulate internal βARs.
source: PI4P hydrolysis initiated by NE was blocked by metoprolol (100 μM, Figure 4A, center) but not sotalol (5 mM, Figure 4A, right) indicating that NE can stimulate internal βARs.
evidence: This is an inference based on the differential effects of membrane-permeant vs impermeant antagonists on NE-induced PI4P hydrolysis.

claim: NE initially stimulated NES-Venus-mini-Gs translocation to the plasma membrane, followed by slower translocation to the Golgi.
source: NE initially stimulated NES-Venus-mini-Gs translocation to the plasma membrane as was observed for dobutamine, followed by slower, NES-Venus-mini-Gs translocation to the Golgi (Figure 4B and Figure 4—video 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: NE enters cardiac myocytes, accesses internal βARs, and stimulates PI4P hydrolysis.
source: Thus, NE enters cardiac myocytes, accesses internal βARs, and stimulates PI4P hydrolysis.
evidence: This is an inference based on the combined experimental data from Figure 4.

claim: Preincubation of NRVMs with corticosterone prevented NE from inducing PI4P hydrolysis.
source: Preincubation of NRVMs with any of these inhibitors prevented NE from inducing PI4P hydrolysis, suggesting that OCT3-mediated transport is required for stimulation of PI4P hydrolysisby this catecholamine.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Preincubation of NRVMs with abacavir prevented NE from inducing PI4P hydrolysis.
source: Preincubation of NRVMs with any of these inhibitors prevented NE from inducing PI4P hydrolysis, suggesting that OCT3-mediated transport is required for stimulation of PI4P hydrolysisby this catecholamine.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Preincubation of NRVMs with lamotrigine prevented NE from inducing PI4P hydrolysis.
source: Preincubation of NRVMs with any of these inhibitors prevented NE from inducing PI4P hydrolysis, suggesting that OCT3-mediated transport is required for stimulation of PI4P hydrolysisby this catecholamine.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: OCT3-mediated transport is required for stimulation of PI4P hydrolysis by NE.
source: Preincubation of NRVMs with any of these inhibitors prevented NE from inducing PI4P hydrolysis, suggesting that OCT3-mediated transport is required for stimulation of PI4P hydrolysisby this catecholamine.
evidence: This is an inference based on the effects of three structurally distinct Oct3 inhibitors blocking NE-induced PI4P hydrolysis.

claim: Dyngo had no effect on NE-mediated PI4P hydrolysis.
source: An inhibitor of dynamin-mediated receptor internalization, Dyngo (40 μM), had no effect on either PI4P hydrolysis (Figure 5D)
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Dyngo had no effect on recruitment of NES-Venus-mini-Gs to the Golgi apparatus by NE.
source: An inhibitor of dynamin-mediated receptor internalization, Dyngo (40 μM), had no effect on either PI4P hydrolysis (Figure 5D) or recruitment of NES-Venus-mini-Gs to the Golgi apparatus (Figure 5E and Figure 5—video 1) by NE.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: Dyngo prevents internalization of FLAG-β1AR at the cell surface.
source: As a positive control, Dyngo does prevent internalization of FLAG-β1AR at the cell surface (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a control experiment supported by data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Corticosterone did not alter cAMP production from cell surface βARs.
source: Additionally, corticosterone (100 μM) did not alter cAMP production from cell surface βARs (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a control experiment supported by data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Corticosterone did not block dobutamine-mediated PI4P hydrolysis but rather enhanced the rate of onset relative to dobutamine alone.
source: Corticosterone did not block dobutamine-mediated PI4P hydrolysis but rather enhanced the rate of onset relative to dobutamine alone (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is a control experiment supported by data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Transport by OCT transporters, not receptor internalization, is required for NE-mediated Golgi βAR activation and PI4P hydrolysis.
source: Together, these data indicate that transport by OCT transporters, not receptor internalization, is required for NE-mediated Golgi βAR activation and PI4P hydrolysis.
evidence: This is an inference based on the combined experimental data from Figure 5.

claim: Following addition of 1 μM Rapamycin, NE-induced PI4P hydrolysis was significantly inhibited.
source: However, following addition of 1 μM Rapamycin, NE-induced PI4P hydrolysis was significantly inhibited (Figure 5F).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5F.

claim: Stimulation of AVMs with dobutamine stimulated PI4P depletion in the Golgi.
source: Stimulation of AVMs with dobutamine (Figure 6B) or NE (Figure 6C) stimulated PI4P depletion in the Golgi.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Stimulation of AVMs with NE stimulated PI4P depletion in the Golgi.
source: Stimulation of AVMs with dobutamine (Figure 6B) or NE (Figure 6C) stimulated PI4P depletion in the Golgi.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: NE-stimulated PI4P hydrolysis in AVMs was blocked by preincubation with the Oct3 inhibitor abacavir.
source: NE-stimulated PI4P hydrolysis was blocked by preincubation with the Oct3 inhibitor abacavir (Figure 6C) indicating that NE transport into AVMs is required for stimulation of PI4P hydrolysis, as was seen in NRVMs.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: NE transport into AVMs is required for stimulation of PI4P hydrolysis.
source: NE-stimulated PI4P hydrolysis was blocked by preincubation with the Oct3 inhibitor abacavir (Figure 6C) indicating that NE transport into AVMs is required for stimulation of PI4P hydrolysis, as was seen in NRVMs.
evidence: This is an inference based on the Oct3 inhibitor blocking NE effects in AVMs.

claim: Internal receptors are required for stimulation of PI4P hydrolysis in AVMs as well as NRVMs.
source: These data indicate that internal receptors are required for stimulation of PI4P hydrolysis in AVMs as well as NRVMs.
evidence: This is an inference based on the combined experimental data from Figure 6.

claim: Dobutamine stimulated an increase in cell area after 48 hr of stimulation.
source: Dobutamine stimulated an increase cell area (Figure 7A), and ANF expression (Figure 7B), after 48 hr of stimulation.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Dobutamine stimulated an increase in ANF expression after 48 hr of stimulation.
source: Dobutamine stimulated an increase cell area (Figure 7A), and ANF expression (Figure 7B), after 48 hr of stimulation.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: Co-incubation with the cell permeant antagonist, metoprolol, strongly inhibited dobutamine-induced increases in cell area and ANF expression.
source: Co-incubation with the cell permeant antagonist, metoprolol, strongly inhibited these hypertrophic responses.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7A and 7B.

claim: The cell impermeant antagonist, sotalol, was significantly less effective at blocking dobutamine-induced cell area increase and ANF expression than metoprolol.
source: The cell impermeant antagonist, sotalol, on the other hand was significantly less effective at blocking these hypertrophy measures than metoprolol, (Figure 7A and B).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7A and 7B.

claim: Internal βARs are involved in mediating cardiomyocyte hypertrophy.
source: These data, taken together with PI4P hydrolysis data, suggest that internal βARs are involved in mediating cardiomyocyte hypertrophy.
evidence: This is an inference based on the differential effects of membrane-permeant vs impermeant antagonists on dobutamine-induced hypertrophy.

claim: Treatment with NE stimulated an increase in cell size.
source: Treatment with NE stimulated an increase in cell size (Figure 8A) and ANF expression (Figure 8B) that was blocked by corticosterone indicating that transport of NE into the myocyte is required to mediate hypertrophy.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8A.

claim: Treatment with NE stimulated an increase in ANF expression.
source: Treatment with NE stimulated an increase in cell size (Figure 8A) and ANF expression (Figure 8B) that was blocked by corticosterone indicating that transport of NE into the myocyte is required to mediate hypertrophy.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8B.

claim: NE-induced increases in cell size and ANF expression were blocked by corticosterone.
source: Treatment with NE stimulated an increase in cell size (Figure 8A) and ANF expression (Figure 8B) that was blocked by corticosterone indicating that transport of NE into the myocyte is required to mediate hypertrophy.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8A and 8B.

claim: Transport of NE into the myocyte is required to mediate hypertrophy.
source: Treatment with NE stimulated an increase in cell size (Figure 8A) and ANF expression (Figure 8B) that was blocked by corticosterone indicating that transport of NE into the myocyte is required to mediate hypertrophy.
evidence: This is an inference based on corticosterone blocking NE-induced hypertrophy.

claim: Treatment with dobutamine induced hypertrophy but this was not blocked by Oct3 inhibition.
source: Treatment with dobutamine also induced hypertrophy but this was not blocked by Oct3 supporting the idea that dobutamine access to internal receptors does not require Oct3 and confirms the specificity of the Oct3 blockade.
evidence: This is a control experiment supported by data shown in Figure 8A and 8B.

claim: Dobutamine access to internal receptors does not require Oct3.
source: Treatment with dobutamine also induced hypertrophy but this was not blocked by Oct3 supporting the idea that dobutamine access to internal receptors does not require Oct3 and confirms the specificity of the Oct3 blockade.
evidence: This is an inference based on the differential effects of Oct3 inhibition on NE vs dobutamine.

claim: Co-treatment with rapamycin blocked NE and dobutamine stimulated hypertrophy.
source: Co-treatment with rapamycin to translocate Nb80 to the Golgi blocked NE and dobutamine stimulated hypertrophy, demonstrating that Golgi βARs are required for stimulation of hypertrophy by these agonists.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8C and 8D.

claim: Golgi βARs are required for stimulation of hypertrophy by NE and dobutamine.
source: Co-treatment with rapamycin to translocate Nb80 to the Golgi blocked NE and dobutamine stimulated hypertrophy, demonstrating that Golgi βARs are required for stimulation of hypertrophy by these agonists.
evidence: This is an inference based on Nb80 translocation to the Golgi blocking NE and dobutamine-induced hypertrophy.

claim: Stimulation of Golgi resident β1ARs induces Epac-PLCε-dependent PI4P hydrolysis when stimulated by either a membrane permeant drug, dobutamine, or the physiological neurotransmitter, norepinephrine.
source: Here we demonstrate that stimulation of Golgi resident β1ARs induces Epac-PLCε-dependent PI4P hydrolysis when stimulated by either a membrane permeant drug, dobutamine, or the physiological neurotransmitter, norepinephrine.
evidence: This is a summary of the primary findings of the study.

claim: Stimulation of internal βARs is required for both dobutamine and NE stimulated cardiomyocyte hypertrophy.
source: We also show that stimulation of these internal receptors is required for both dobutamine and NE stimulated cardiomyocyte hypertrophy.
evidence: This is a summary of the primary findings of the study.

claim: GPCRs can be found on intracellular compartments.
source: It is well established that GPCRs can be found on intracellular compartments (Jong et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: GPCRs have been characterized on the nuclear envelope in neurons and cardiac myocytes.
source: A number of investigators have characterized GPCRs on the nuclear envelope in neurons and cardiac myocytes, and signaling mechanisms have been proposed (Kumar et al., 2008; Boivin et al., 2006; Merlen et al., 2013; Dahl et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: GPCRs and G proteins have been found on the Golgi apparatus.
source: GPCRs and G proteins have been found on other intracellular compartments including the Golgi apparatus, but signaling roles for receptors at the Golgi are not well defined.
evidence: This is supported by general knowledge in the field.

claim: Signaling roles for receptors at the Golgi are not well defined.
source: GPCRs and G proteins have been found on other intracellular compartments including the Golgi apparatus, but signaling roles for receptors at the Golgi are not well defined.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge in the field.

claim: GPCRs are trafficked through the Golgi apparatus on their way to the cell surface.
source: This is in part because GPCRs are trafficked through the Golgi apparatus on their way to the cell surface and it has not been clear that GPCRs in the Golgi have a signaling function.
evidence: This is supported by established knowledge of GPCR trafficking.

claim: Irannejad et al. (2017) definitively demonstrated that Golgi localized β1ARs and Gs can be driven to an active conformation by exogenous ligands.
source: The recent work by Irannejad et al. (2017) definitively demonstrated that Golgi localized β1ARs and Gs can be driven to an active conformation by exogenous ligands.
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: The thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH) receptor activates Gs in the Golgi in mouse thyroid cells through a mechanism that relies on endosomal retrograde trafficking of internalized receptors.
source: Recent work from the Calebiro laboratory demonstrated that the thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH) receptor activates Gs in the Golgi in mouse thyroid cells through a mechanism that relies on endosomal retrograde trafficking of internalized receptors (Godbole et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: Activation of Golgi β1ARs in cardiac myocytes does not involve receptor internalization but rather relies on Golgi resident receptors and transport of ligands across the cell membrane via Oct3.
source: This is in contrast to what is shown here in cardiac myocytes, and as reported by Irannejad et al. in Hela cells, where activation of Golgi β1ARs does not involve receptor internalization but rather relies on Golgi resident receptors and transport of ligands across the cell membrane via Oct3.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data.

claim: The purpose of internal GPCR signaling is likely to generate signals that are local and distinct from receptors at the PM or other intracellular locations.
source: The purpose of internal GPCR signaling is likely to generate signals that are local and distinct from receptors at the PM or other intracellular locations.
evidence: This is speculation about the biological significance of internal GPCR signaling.

claim: During acute sympathetic stimulation, norepinephrine may only access cell surface βARs needed to mediate increases in cardiac contraction required to meet the demands of a sympathetic response.
source: In the case of the cardiac myocyte, during acute sympathetic stimulation, norepinephrine may only access cell surface βARs needed to mediate increases in cardiac contraction required to meet the demands of a sympathetic response.
evidence: This is speculation about the physiological role of compartmentalized signaling.

claim: Signaling by Golgi βARs requires uptake of ligand prior to activation, so these processes are slower and may not be accessed during acute sympathetic responses, but rather are only activated during more chronic exposure such as is observed in cardiovascular stress.
source: Because signaling by Golgi βARs requires uptake of ligand prior to activation, these processes are slower and may not be accessed during acute sympathetic responses, but rather are only activated during more chronic exposure such as is observed in cardiovascular stress.
evidence: This is speculation about the physiological role of Golgi βAR signaling.

claim: Separation of the Epac/mAKAPβ/PLCε pathway at the nuclear envelope/Golgi interface from global cAMP dependent PKA activation possibly prevents inappropriate activation of PLCε dependent hypertrophic responses to acute βAR activation.
source: Separation of the Epac/mAKAPβ/PLCε pathway at the nuclear envelope/Golgi interface from global cAMP dependent PKA activation possibly prevents inappropriate activation of PLCε dependent hypertrophic responses to acute βAR activation.
evidence: This is speculation about the functional significance of compartmentalized signaling.

claim: Stimulation of hypertrophy by the natural sympathetic ligand NE required activity of Golgi localized βARs.
source: Significantly, stimulation of hypertrophy by the natural sympathetic ligand NE required activity of Golgi localized βARs.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data.

claim: Sustained elevated sympathetic drive is one of the major factors responsible for development of cardiac hypertrophy due to chronic hypertension.
source: As has been discussed, sustained elevated sympathetic drive is one of the major factors responsible for development of cardiac hypertrophy due to chronic hypertension.
evidence: This is supported by established knowledge in cardiovascular pathophysiology.

claim: β-blocker therapy efficacy is thought to result from preventing chronic stimulation of cell surface βARs by elevated catecholamines and subsequent desensitization.
source: β-blocker therapy efficacy is thought to result from preventing chronic stimulation of cell surface βARs by elevated catecholamines and subsequent desensitization (Bristow, 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: Blockade of internal receptors may be required to prevent catecholamine-induced hypertrophy.
source: Our results suggest that blockade of internal receptors may be required to prevent catecholamine-induced hypertrophy and demonstrates that activation of cell surface GPCRs is not sufficient for natural catecholamines to induce hypertrophy in NRVMs.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data showing internal receptors are required for NE-induced hypertrophy.

claim: Activation of cell surface GPCRs is not sufficient for natural catecholamines to induce hypertrophy in NRVMs.
source: Our results suggest that blockade of internal receptors may be required to prevent catecholamine-induced hypertrophy and demonstrates that activation of cell surface GPCRs is not sufficient for natural catecholamines to induce hypertrophy in NRVMs.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data showing internal receptors are required for NE-induced hypertrophy.

claim: The cell permeant βAR antagonist metoprolol is significantly more effective than the cell impermeant antagonist sotalol in prevention of dobutamine stimulated cardiomyocyte hypertrophy.
source: The importance of blockade of Golgi GPCRs is supported by the fact that the cell permeant βAR antagonist metoprolol is significantly more effective than the cell impermeant antagonist sotalol in prevention of dobutamine stimulated cardiomyocyte hypertrophy.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data.

claim: Clinically effective β-blockers tend to be relatively hydrophobic.
source: Interestingly, clinically effective β-blockers tend to be relatively hydrophobic.
evidence: This is supported by knowledge of clinical pharmacology.

claim: Metoprolol and carvedilol are first line β blockers that are used to treat heart failure and have log P values 1.8 and 4.2 respectively, and are thus relatively cell permeant.
source: Metoprolol and carvedilol are first line β blockers that are used to treat heart failure and have log P values 1.8 and 4.2 respectively, and are thus relatively cell permeant.
evidence: This is supported by knowledge of clinical pharmacology and drug properties.

claim: Sotalol has a log P of −0.85, is relatively cell impermeant, and is not clinically used for heart failure treatment.
source: Sotalol, which has a log P of −0.85 is relatively cell impermeant, and is not clinically used for heart failure treatment.
evidence: This is supported by knowledge of clinical pharmacology and drug properties.

claim: Hydrophobicity might be an important factor for β-blocker development allowing these inhibitors to access internal pools of receptor.
source: We speculate that hydrophobicity might be an important factor for β-blocker development allowing these inhibitors to access internal pools of receptor.
evidence: This is speculation based on the correlation between hydrophobicity and clinical efficacy.

claim: The cell impermeant agonist isoproterenol induces hypertrophy in vitro and when chronically administered in vivo.
source: A seeming contradiction is the observation that the cell impermeant agonist isoproterenol induces hypertrophy in vitro and when chronically administered in vivo (Zhang et al., 2011; Iaccarino et al., 1998).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Iso administered in vivo is not at physiological concentrations and has multiple target tissues beyond the cardiac myocyte, such as the vasculature, that could contribute to hypertrophy.
source: Iso administered in vivo is not at physiological concentrations and has multiple target tissues beyond the cardiac myocyte, such as the vasculature, that could contribute to hypertrophy.
evidence: This is speculation about the mechanisms of Iso-induced hypertrophy in vivo.

claim: While Iso can induce hypertrophy in NRVMs in vitro by a mechanism that probably does not rely on internal receptors, the effects of the natural ligands epinephrine and norepinephrine are more relevant to the in vivo situation and do rely on Golgi localized βARs.
source: For NRVMs in vitro, while Iso can induce hypertrophy by a mechanism that probably does not rely on internal receptors, the effects of the natural ligands epinephrine and norepinephrine are more relevant to the in vivo situation and do rely on Golgi localized βARs.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data showing differential mechanisms for Iso vs NE.

claim: The synthetic agonist Iso seems to rely on an alternative PM mediated pathway that is not engaged by the physiological agonist NE.
source: The synthetic agonist Iso seems to rely on an alternative PM mediated pathway that is not engaged by the physiological agonist NE.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data showing differential mechanisms for Iso vs NE.

claim: Endogenous β1ARs are present at the Golgi in cardiac myocytes.
source: as has been previously reported, we were able to detect staining of endogenous β1ARs at the Golgi in cardiac myocytes (Figure 1—figure supplement 1)
evidence: This is supported by immunocytochemistry data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Dobutamine addition to cells co-expressing NES-Venus-mini-Gs and FLAG-β1AR caused rapid clearance of cytoplasmic fluorescence and accumulated fluorescence at the PM and punctate structures, possibly corresponding to microtubules.
source: Addition of dobutamine to cells co-expressing NES-Venus-mini-Gs and FLAG-β1AR, caused a rapid clearance of cytoplasmic fluorescence and accumulated fluorescence at the PM and punctate structures, possibly corresponding to microtubules.
evidence: This is a primary observation from the imaging experiments with speculation about the identity of punctate structures.

claim: Upon addition of rapamycin, translocation of CFP-Nb80-FRB to the Golgi apparatus was observed.
source: Upon addition of rapamycin, translocation of CFP-Nb80-FRB to the Golgi apparatus was observed (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is a primary observation supported by imaging data shown in Figure 3A.
